{{short description|Two-dimensional packing problem}}

'''Circle packing in a circle''' is a two-dimensional [[packing problem]] with the objective of packing [[unit circle]]s into the smallest possible larger [[circle]].

{{TOC limit|3}}<!--To avoid layout breaking when TOC is hidden-->

== Table of solutions, 1 ≤ ''n'' ≤ 20 ==

==Special cases==
Only 26 optimal packings are thought to be rigid (with no circles able to "rattle"). Numbers in '''bold''' are prime:
* Proven for ''n'' = 1, '''2''', '''3''', 4, '''5''', 6, '''7''', 10, '''11''', 12, '''13''', 14, '''19'''
* Conjectured for ''n'' = 15, 16, '''17''', 18, 22, '''23''', 27, 30, '''31''', 33, '''37''', '''61''', 91
Of these, solutions for ''n'' = '''2''', '''3''', 4, '''7''', '''19''', and '''37''' achieve a packing density greater than any smaller number > 1. (Higher density records all have rattles.)<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A084644}}</ref>
